bounds.reflection:
The previous iteration (Mulch 20.0, DAP 150.0, Sown 04-Jul) resulted in a yield of 1750 kg/ha, but highlighted significant stress in Nitrogen and Water during the critical reproductive stages, despite the land prep. The simulator specifically flagged high nitrate leaching (31.1kg/ha NO3) and suggested adding a split or foliar N after heavy percolation. This indicates that while the basal DAP was applied, the nutrient management structure needs to be more robust to handle leaching risk, especially given the variable monsoon nature. 

Given the early sowing date (Jul 4th) and the current dry spell, a moderate level of initial soil moisture retention (Mulch) and adequate P availability (DAP) is crucial for establishment. I will slightly increase the bounds for both to ensure better early vigor.

For the season-wide structure, the feedback strongly suggests the need for flexible N management to compensate for leaching. Therefore, I must allow for more urea splits than perhaps initially planned, but I must balance this against the 'do not budget heavily when the monsoon outlook is wet' guideline. Since the monsoon is patchy (68mm total so far), I need a flexible system. I will set a reasonable upper limit on urea splits (e.g., 3-4) to allow for mid-season top-ups if rainfall fails, but I will keep the minimum dose high enough to be economically meaningful for a smallholder.

Regarding irrigation, the high leaching risk suggests that we should not be overly conservative, but we must respect the climate resilience guideline. I will allow for a moderate number of irrigation events, ensuring the ceiling is high enough to buffer against mid-season dry spells, but not so high that it negates the need for rain-fed resilience. The minimum irrigation dose should reflect the need to address localized water stress.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

The results revealed that foliar spray of Fluopyrum 21.37% w/w + Trifloxystrobin 21.37%
---
Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.
---

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.

Why ammonical nitrogen fertilizers are more suited for paddy cultivation? Ø Rice is the only crop which can utilize the ammonical nitrogen. Ø They are less readily available to plants than nitrate fertilizers. The ammonical nitrogen has to nitrify in the soil and be converted into nitrate before it can be taken up by plants. Ø The ammonia in ammonium sulphate is fixed (adsorbed) by the soil immediately after application and it is not leached away like nitrates. Ø Hence, this group of fertilizers may be used in basal application and top dressing.
